Key Topic 3 • Attempts at Peace, 1974–95

KT 3.4: Attempts at a Solution: From the Oslo Accords to Oslo II (1993–95): Forensic Analysis & Word Bank

Deep Knowledge
Forensic Case Studies
1. The Gulf War Financial Disaster & Soviet Aliyah
  • Arafat's Gulf War Blunder: By publicly embracing Saddam Hussein during the 1990 invasion of Kuwait, Arafat alienated wealthy Gulf monarchies; upon liberation, Kuwait expelled 400,000 Palestinian workers.
  • Financial Ruin: The PLO lost $100 million annually in Arab subsidies and worker remittances, bankrupting its institutions, schools, and hospitals, leaving Arafat desperate for a diplomatic breakthrough to retain power.
2. The Oslo Secret Negotiations & Mutual Recognition
  • Norwegian Discretion: Norwegian social scientist Terje Rød-Larsen and Foreign Minister Johan Jørgen Holst organized 14 secret meetings in rural Norwegian mansions, shielding negotiators from public pressure.
  • Breaking Taboos: For the first time, Israeli officials sat directly with PLO leaders; they bypassed thorny final-status issues (Jerusalem, refugees, borders) to achieve an interim breakthrough based on "land for peace".
3. The Oslo II West Bank Division (Areas A, B, C)
  • Area A (3% of West Bank): Encompassed the 8 major Palestinian cities (Jenin, Nablus, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Ramallah, Bethlehem, Jericho, Hebron); full PA civil administration and internal security control.
  • Area B (25% of West Bank): Covered 450 Palestinian rural towns and villages (approx. 68% of Palestinian population); PA exercised civil administration, but the IDF retained overriding military security control.
4. The Extremist Sabotage & Rabin's Assassination
  • Hamas & Islamic Jihad Suicide Bombings: Militant Islamists opposed conceding Islamic waqf land; suicide bombings in Afula, Hadera, and Tel Aviv commuter buses killed dozens of civilians, turning Israeli public opinion against Oslo.
  • Hebron Mosque Massacre (25 Feb 1994): US-born Jewish extremist Baruch Goldstein opened fire with an assault rifle inside the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, murdering 29 Palestinian worshippers during morning Ramadan prayers.
Causal Pathway: Key Historical Mechanisms Cause & Consequence Chain
1. Geneva 1988 & Gulf Crisis Arafat renounces terrorism; backing Saddam alienates Gulf states; Kuwait expels 400k Palestinians; PLO goes bankrupt.
2. Soviet Aliyah & Secret Oslo 600k Soviet Jews arrive; Holst hosts secret Norwegian channel; Israel & PLO exchange mutual recognition in 1993.
3. Oslo I & Jordan Treaty White House handshake; PA established in Gaza-Jericho; Jordan signs formal peace treaty with Israel in Oct 1994.
4. Oslo II & Rabin Murder (1995) West Bank split into Areas A (3%), B (25%), C (72%); Hamas bus bombings; Yigal Amir assassinates Rabin on 4 Nov 1995.

Master Cartographic Atlas • The Territorial Revolution

Plate 3: The 1967 Six Day War & The Occupied Territories

Atlas Study 2
Strategic Transformation: Between 5 and 10 June 1967, Israel launched pre-emptive air strikes (Operation Focus) obliterating Egypt's air force, followed by a sweeping tri-front ground offensive. In just six days, Israel shattered the armies of Egypt, Jordan, and Syria, capturing territory more than three times its original size and creating the Occupied Territories.
The Five Captured Territories & UN Security Council Resolution 242
1. The Five Occupied Territories:
• Sinai Peninsula (from Egypt): 60,000 km² desert buffer zone extending to the Suez Canal; Sharm el-Sheikh reopened Straits of Tiran.
• Gaza Strip (from Egypt): 360 km² narrow coastal enclave packed with 350,000 Palestinian refugees.
• West Bank & East Jerusalem (from Jordan): 5,600 km² containing 600,000 Palestinians; East Jerusalem annexed immediately.
• Golan Heights (from Syria): 1,200 km² strategic plateau dominating the Sea of Galilee and Damascus approaches.
2. UN Resolution 242 (22 Nov 1967): "Land for Peace":
• Clause 1(i): "Withdrawal of Israel armed forces from territories occupied in the recent conflict" (deliberately omitted the word "the" in English).
• Clause 1(ii): Termination of all claims of belligerency; respect for sovereignty and right to live in peace within secure, recognized borders.
• Long-term Dilemma: Israel gained defensible borders and strategic depth, but absorbed over 1 million hostile Palestinian Arabs under military rule.
Khartoum Resolution (Sept 1967): Arab League issued the famous "Three No's": No peace with Israel, No recognition of Israel, No negotiations with Israel.

Master Cartographic Atlas • The Geopolitical Division

Plate 4: The 1993–1995 Oslo Accords & West Bank Partition

Atlas Study 2
Diplomatic Breakthrough & Territorial Fragmentation: Brokered secretly in Norway, the 1993 Oslo I Accord established mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO, creating the Palestinian National Authority (PNA). In September 1995, the Oslo II Agreement (Taba Accord) divided the West Bank into three separate administrative zones as a transitional 5-year step towards permanent peace.
Green: Area A • Dark Red: Area B • Light Red: Area C
AREA A: Full Palestinian Control (Green)
• Territory: Initially only 3% of the West Bank (expanded to ~18% by 1999).
• Jurisdiction: Palestinian Authority has full civil and internal security control.
• Population: Encompasses major Arab population centers: Ramallah, Nablus, Jenin, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Bethlehem, Jericho, and Hebron.
AREA B: Joint Administrative Control (Dark Red)
• Territory: Approximately 25% of the West Bank (expanded to ~22%).
• Jurisdiction: Palestinian civil administration; Israeli overriding military security control.
• Geography: Covers ~450 Palestinian villages and rural farmland surrounding Area A cities.
AREA C: Full Israeli Military Control (Light Red)
• Territory: Contiguous 72% of the West Bank (later ~60%).
• Jurisdiction: Complete Israeli civil and military control (planning, building permits, security).
• Strategic Value: Contains all 140,000+ Israeli settlers, bypass roads, military bases, and the Jordan Valley border strip. Palestinian areas became disconnected "islands".
The Fatal Flaw: Deferred Final Status Issues
Oslo postponed the 4 most contentious questions: (1) Jerusalem sovereignty, (2) Right of return for 1948 refugees, (3) Settler dismantling, and (4) Independent statehood. In Nov 1995, Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated by Jewish extremist Yigal Amir, plunging the peace process into crisis.

Historiography • Academic Perspectives • Grade 9 Evaluative Mastery

Master Historiographical Debates: Traditional vs New Historians

Grade 9 Mastery
Historiographical Overview: The Evolution of Middle Eastern Historical Debate
High-achieving students distinguish between Traditional Zionist/Arab historiography and the critical "New Historians" who emerged after Israeli state archives were declassified under the 30-year rule in the late 1980s. Understanding these competing interpretations allows students to provide nuanced, evaluative judgments in Paper 2 Question 3 (Importance).
Debate 1: Causes of the 1948 Palestinian Refugee Exodus (Al-Nakba)
Traditional Zionist Narrative: Arab leaders broadcast radio orders urging civilians to flee temporarily to clear the path for invading Arab armies, promising a swift return after victory.
"New Historian" Critique (Benny Morris): Declassified IDF documents revealed no broadcast orders; refugees fled due to military assaults, Plan Dalet expulsions, and terror following the Deir Yassin massacre.
Debate 2: Responsibility for the 1967 Six Day War
Israeli Pre-emptive Defence View: Nasser's expulsion of UNEF, closure of the Straits of Tiran (an act of war), and mobilization of 100,000 troops created an existential threat justifying pre-emptive strikes.
Revisionist / Pan-Arab View: Nasser was engaged in political brinkmanship without an offensive plan; Israeli military leadership exploited Arab rhetoric to capture the West Bank, Golan Heights, and East Jerusalem.
Debate 3: The Failure of the 1993 Oslo Peace Process
Pro-Israeli Perspective: Arafat and the PNA failed to dismantle terrorist networks (Hamas and Islamic Jihad suicide bombings), proving the Palestinian leadership was unwilling to guarantee Israeli security.
Pro-Palestinian Perspective (Edward Said): Oslo was an instrument of Palestinian capitulation; Israeli settlement expansion doubled in the West Bank while leaving core issues (Jerusalem, refugees, borders) unresolved.
